subject: Streaming responsiveness incident — customer playbook and next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Bell <dana.bell@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming responsiveness incident — initial notice

Hi Dana,

We observed a degradation in streaming responsiveness affecting some chat sessions between ~08:55–09:05 PDT this morning. The root cause appears related to a transient queuing behavior on a small subset of GPU backplanes that increased per-token serialization time for streaming connections.

Impact: intermittent slower stream chunks (pauses of ~300–900ms) for a subset (~2%) of long-running conversations. No dropped tokens or incorrect outputs were observed.

Immediate mitigations we put in place:
- Enabled short-term routing around the affected pool (automatic fallback to warm-edge nodes).
- Reduced max-stream-buffer size from 64KB to 32KB to smooth chunking during the incident window.

Recommended customer actions (short term):
1) If you need strict latency bounds for critical flows, temporarily switch these endpoints to non-streaming (polling) mode for the next 2 hours while we stabilize routing.
2) Add exponential backoff on your client retry (start 75ms, cap 800ms) for chunk-reassembly timeouts.
3) Optional: enable the "chunked_streaming_fallback" flag (we can toggle per-account) — this forces the server to send conservative chunk sizes and reduces pause spikes.

I've attached a short runbook and a mutual action plan; Evelyn and Sean are looped for technical follow-up and any immediate toggles. We'll send a post-incident summary within 24 hours.

Apologies for the disruption — we know responsiveness matters for your care workflows.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Customer Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: incident_runbook_v2.pdf (pdf)]
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dana Bell <dana.bell@omnihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responsiveness incident — initial notice

Thanks Stephanie — quick ops note:

- We've pushed a temporary scheduling tweak to avoid the affected backplanes and increased the concurrency window on warm-edge nodes by 12% (INF-4912).
- Telemetry indicates the pause events correlate with shard-reshuffle events that occurred during a rolling redispatch. That redispatch was initiated to reclaim fragmented GPU memory after a separate maintenance task this morning.

Short-term customer guidance I'd add: reduce client-side max chunk buffer to 20–32KB and consider using a 1.1s client-side chunk reassembly timeout (we'll still deliver tokens; you will see slightly larger chunks).

I'll start a targeted log grab for OmniHealth sessions between 08:45–09:15 and share sanitized traces.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Runtime Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Dana Bell <dana.bell@omnihealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Mercado <alex.mercado@omnihealth.com>, support@omnihealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responsiveness incident — initial notice

Thanks for the quick heads-up, Stephanie / Evelyn. We saw user complaints around 08:58 and queued a dashboard alert at 09:01.

Action on our side: we temporarily routed the clinical chat escalation flow to non-streaming endpoints per your recommendation and put a rate cap on non-critical background requests. Please send the traces when available — we need them for our incident log and to brief Ops.

Please keep us posted on when the routing and scheduling changes are reverted.

—Dana
Dana Bell
SRE Manager, OmniHealth
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Bell <dana.bell@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responsiveness incident — customer playbook & next steps

Dana —

We collected the traces and sanitized them; a summary is attached and I've included the runbook with explicit playbook steps for your engineering team. Key next steps we will take (by EOD):
- Complete the shard placement rollback and run an integrity check on the affected pool (target 14:30 PDT).
- Run a short burst test (internal) to validate chunking stability and re-enable normal buffer sizes if we see no regressions.
- Postmortem and TOC (timeline, root cause, mitigations, follow-ups) posted to the Drive link below.

Attachment: omni_health_mutual_action_plan.xlsx — includes owner matrix for any toggles you need to request from us and which flags we can flip as an account-level override.

If you want, Monica from Customer Success can schedule a 30-min run-through of the playbook with your on-call engineers so you can rehearse toggles and rollbacks.

Best,
Stephanie
[Attachment: omni_health_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Dana Bell <dana.bell@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responsiveness incident — validation results

Dana / Stephanie — quick technical update:

- We completed the rollback and integrity checks at 14:05 PDT. No replay mismatches found.
- Warm-edge churn decreased to baseline; pause events dropped to <0.1% in the subsequent 2-hour window.
- We tested client configurations: enabling chunked_streaming_fallback plus max chunk size 28KB yielded the most consistent completion latency in our internal bench.

We'll keep monitoring for 24 hours and will notify you before we revert temporary flags. Leaving the account-level fallback enabled until tomorrow 09:00 PDT unless you request earlier.

—Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Dana Bell <dana.bell@omnihealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming responsiveness incident — confirmation and thank you

Thanks — we appreciate the fast remediation and the playbook. Monica, please schedule the run-through for tomorrow morning at 09:30 PDT.

We'll keep our fallback to non-streaming for the critical escalation flow until you confirm the account flags are cleared. Please share the postmortem link and any action items after your 24-hour review.

—Dana
